subtopic: Insured Bank and Credit Union Deposits
source_evidence: Your money may be insured by the Federal Deposit Insurance Corporation (FDIC) or National Credit Union Administration (NCUA).
answer: Savings accounts, checking accounts, and certificates of deposit are examples of places people can keep savings. Money in these accounts may be insured by the FDIC or NCUA, which can provide a measure of security. Savings also typically trade higher earnings for security and access: the source notes that savings earn a low interest rate.
